1.explanation: The missing‐tile gap appears because the reprojection engine splits each target tile into triangles/quads in the source projection (Triangulation), but the logic that detects and shifts coordinates across the ±180° wrap is too conservative. In `Triangulation`'s constructor it may refuse to shift triangles when the extent spans the prime meridian and dateline, and in `addQuad_` it doesn’t correctly subdivide quads crossing the wrap. As a result, source‐projection areas on the ‘other side’ of the antimeridian aren’t covered by any triangles. In addition, `ReprojTile.reproject_` uses the triangulation and source tiles to draw onto a canvas; if triangles are missing then rendering omits those regions. Fixing the wrap‐X detection and quad subdivision in `Triangulation` (and ensuring `ReprojTile` uses the wrapped tile coordinate to compute extents) will allow tiles to render seamlessly across the antimeridian.
1.bug_scenario: When reprojecting a GeoTIFF into a stereographic projection and displaying it in a WebGLTileLayer, tiles that cross the antimeridian (the ±180° longitude seam) are not rendered. The map shows a black gap along the dateline because the reprojection triangulation fails to generate triangles across the world‐wrap boundary.

2.explanation: Triangulation is responsible for subdividing each target tile into triangles (and quads) and mapping them back to the source projection. Its addQuad_ and addTriangle_ methods contain special logic to detect and shift extents that cross the projection’s wrap-around meridian (using modulo arithmetic). A flaw in this wrapping/shifting logic near the antimeridian causes no triangles to be generated for that slice of the target extent, so renderReprojected in ReprojTile.reproject_ has no geometry to draw—producing the visible gaps. Fixing or improving the handling in Triangulation.addQuad_/addTriangle_ (and related modulo calculations) ensures continuous coverage across the dateline.
2.bug_scenario: When reprojection of GeoTIFF tiles to a custom stereographic projection crosses the antimeridian, WebGLTileLayer fails to generate or render the necessary triangles on the far side of the dateline. As a result, you see black gaps (missing tiles) along the antimeridian boundary, whose size varies with tile size and zoom level.
